newsitem.title: USA: Disney/ABC in TV pact with Germany's Kirch.
newsitem.headline: Disney/ABC in TV pact with Germany's Kirch.

text.p: Disney/ABC International, a unit of Walt Disney Co., and the KirchGroup of Germany said Thursday they signed an exclusive, 10-year pay television agreement covering all Disney live-action movies.
The pact also calls for development of a premium Disney Channel specificially for Germany, the companies said.
No value was placed on the agreement, and a spokeswoman for Disney was not immediately available.

Kirch last month agreed to pay $1 billion for long-term pay-TV rights to films from MCA, a unit of Seagram Co., and has also signed a long-term deal with Viacom, another leading U.S. entertainment group.
Kirch, a leading media company in Germany, last month launched a new television service called DF1. Its chairman, Leo Kirch, was quoted as saying the Disney films would be shown on that service.
"Particularly important in this respect is the prospect of carrying The Disney Channel itself," Kirch said.
Disney said it will retain full ownership of the German version of The Disney Channel, a family-oriented cable television service long established in the United States.
The Disney Channel will be sold as a premimum service in Germany.
There are also tailored versions of The Disney Channel in Taiwan, Australia and Britain.

Disney, which acquired the ABC Television network a year ago, already has substantial European TV interests, including 50 percent of Super RTL, 37.5 percent of cable-service TM3, and 23 percent of RTL2.
Its live-action film studios include Disney, Hollywood and Touchstone.
Disney's stock lost 50 cents to $57.875 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
